finding.claim: Workbook zip entry names are passed unvalidated into the output zip (zip-slip pass-through). A crafted input entry such as ../../x or /x is re-emitted verbatim on Save/WriteTo, so a consumer that later extracts the re-saved file unsafely can write outside its target directory.
finding.source: Input zip entry name (lib.go:55-61 via ReadZipReader; excelize.go:228-230 Pkg.Store). Only backslash is rewritten to slash.
finding.sink: zw.Create(path) with the Pkg key written verbatim (file.go:201-218; same for tempFiles keys at file.go:227-230).

trace.note: fileName = ReplaceAll(v.Name, backslash, slash); the only normalization applied
fileList[fileName] = readFile(v); unknown names kept as-is
for k, v := range file { f.Pkg.Store(k, v) }
Pkg.Range collects every key into files; no path check
zw.Create(path) uses the attacker-chosen name unchanged

finding.guards_checked: Only backslash-to-slash rewrite (lib.go:61). docPart remaps two fixed names (lib.go:47-50, 62-64). No filepath.Clean, IsLocal, '..' or leading-slash rejection in read or write path. Precondition: app opens untrusted xlsx and saves or re-serves it, and a downstream consumer extracts unsafely. Not verified: whether archive/zip Writer rejects such names.

finding.claim: Default decompression limit is about 16.8 GB (templates.go:195, 1000<<24) and is checked only against declared entry sizes. A small crafted zip can make excelize preallocate and then fully decompress large non-sheet parts into RAM, or spool sheet parts to disk, exhausting memory or disk.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied xlsx whose entries declare UncompressedSize64 up to the limit (per entry and in total).
finding.sink: make([]byte, 0, declaredSize) before any data is read (lib.go:162), then unbounded io.Copy into memory (lib.go:164); oversized sheet parts spooled to disk via unzipToTemp (lib.go:76-83, 95-111).

trace.note: UnzipSizeLimit = 1000 << 24 (about 16.8 GB)
default options.UnzipSizeLimit applied when unset
checkFileSize compares declared sizes to the limit
unzipSize accumulates declared sizes across entries
non-sheet entries go to readFile
preallocates declared size before reading
io.Copy into RAM; no cap beyond declared size

finding.guards_checked: Per-file and total declared-size checks (lib.go:33-40, 56-60) with a default limit so high it is effectively no limit. Sheet parts over StreamChunkSize (16 MiB, templates.go:191) are spooled to disk with no disk-size cap. Assumes archive/zip caps actual output at declared size (not verified in source). Deflate ratios can make a small file expand to the declared size.

finding.claim: Malformed encrypted (OLE/CFB) input panics on unchecked slice indexing. No recover() exists in the package, so the calling process crashes. This happens before any password check, so no password is needed.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied file with OLE magic header; EncryptionInfo stream with version 3.2, 4.2 or 2.x but short or inconsistent contents; or missing or short EncryptedPackage stream.
finding.sink: Go slice index panics: encryptionInfoBuf[8:12] and block slicing (crypt.go:244-255); blob slicing in standardEncryptionVerifier (crypt.go:290-299); encryptedPackageBuf[8:] (crypt.go:274); x[bs:be] when ciphertext length is not a multiple of 16 (crypt.go:281-283).

trace.note: OLE header detected; Decrypt called unconditionally, regardless of Password
Decrypt entry point
extractPart checks only maximum stream size, not minimum
encryptionMechanism requires len>=4 only; version 4.2 or 3.2 -> standard
encryptionInfoBuf[8:12]: panics if len<12
block := encryptionInfoBuf[12:12+size]: panics if size exceeds buffer
block[32:]: panics if short
standardEncryptionVerifier slices blob[:4], blob[40:72]: panics if short
encryptedPackageBuf[8:]: panics if stream missing or <8 bytes
x[bs:be] panics when len(x) is not a multiple of 16

finding.guards_checked: extractPart enforces entry.Size <= maxStreamSize (crypt.go:202). No minimum-length or structural checks on EncryptionInfo or EncryptedPackage. No recover() in package. Panic occurs before any password or key check.

finding.claim: REPT builds its output with no size cap, so a formula with a large count allocates and loops unboundedly. Formulas in untrusted workbooks can be evaluated by a read-only API, so this is a memory and CPU DoS.
finding.source: Formula text in a cell <f> element of an untrusted workbook. Reachable via CalcCellValue, and via GetPictureCells / GetPictures for any cell whose formula starts with DISPIMG.
finding.sink: bytes.Buffer loop: for i < int(times.Number) { buf.WriteString(text) } (calc.go:14445-14448).

trace.note: GetPictureCells, public read API
getImageCells called on sheet read
formula prefix DISPIMG check
CalcCellValue evaluates the formula
times = ToNumber of second argument
only negative and zero are rejected
unbounded loop writes times copies

finding.guards_checked: Type checks, negative and zero cases (calc.go:14432-14444). No output-length or count limit. Assumes DISPIMG arguments are evaluated before its own type check (standard evaluator flow; evalInfixExp not traced in full). Calc iteration cap (calc.go:1824) limits cycles, not allocation size.

finding.claim: Form-control text is written into the VML part without XML escaping, so attacker-supplied text can break well-formedness or inject markup into the output.
finding.source: FormControl.Text (vml.go:607-608) and FormControl.Paragraph[].Text (vml.go:610-612), supplied by the application, e.g. user-entered labels.
finding.sink: vmlFont.Content tagged xml:",innerxml" (vmlDrawing.go:146-151), emitted raw into xl/drawings/vmlDrawingN.vml.

trace.note: AddFormControl -> addVMLObject
formCtrlText builds vmlFont values
FormControl.Text stored unescaped in Content

run.Text + '

' concatenated; wrapped in // at 624-633 by string concatenation
sp.TextBox.Div.Font = formCtrlText(opts)
innerxml tag: string written verbatim into the VML XML

finding.guards_checked: No escaping in vml.go (no xml.EscapeText or html escape). Comment rich text is safe: it uses typed xlsxR structs (vml.go:313-319). Font attributes (Face, Color) are attributes and encoded by encoding/xml. Runtime effect not verified; '&' or '<' should make the VML malformed.

finding.claim: SearchSheet compiles the search value as a regex unconditionally, so a plain-text search containing regex metacharacters (for example '(', '[', '*') panics via MustCompile.
finding.source: The value argument to SearchSheet(sheet, value), e.g. user-typed search text; regSearch=false does not skip the compile.
finding.sink: regexp.MustCompile(value) (sheet.go:1133), which panics on invalid patterns.

trace.note: SearchSheet public API
passes value and regSearch to searchSheet
MustCompile runs before the loop, regardless of regSearch
regex only used when regSearch is true

finding.guards_checked: checkSheetName only (sheet.go:1103). No regexp.QuoteMeta for plain search and no error-returning Compile. Repro: SearchSheet("Sheet1", "(") panics even though it is a plain-text search.

finding.claim: Image and background helpers read any local file at a caller-given path and embed its bytes into the output workbook. Only the path extension is checked, so an app that forwards an untrusted path lets the attacker read local files whose names end in an allowed image extension.
finding.source: Caller-supplied path to SetSheetBackground (sheet.go:528-535) or AddPicture (picture.go:195-206), e.g. a user-chosen file path.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(path)) (sheet.go:534; picture.go:205); contents are embedded into the saved workbook.

trace.note: os.Stat existence check only
os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(picture)); read error discarded
setSheetBackground(path.Ext(picture), bytes)
AddPicture: extension allowlist check on name
os.ReadFile(filepath.Clean(name)); read error discarded

finding.guards_checked: os.Stat existence check; extension allowlist (picture.go:201). Content is not checked against the extension. No directory confinement. Precondition: the application forwards an attacker-chosen path. Severity is low because the attacker sees only image-extension files, and only via the output file.

finding.claim: Duplicate zip entry names overwrite the tempFiles map, so earlier spooled temp files are never removed by Close and remain on disk.
finding.source: Crafted xlsx with two sheet or sharedStrings entries that share a name (after backslash normalization) and exceed UnzipXMLSizeLimit.
finding.sink: f.tempFiles.Store(fileName, tempFile) overwrites the earlier path (lib.go:66-68, 77-79); Close removes only the mapped paths (file.go:100-105).

trace.note: unzipToTemp creates a temp file for the first entry
tempFiles.Store(fileName, tempFile)
second entry with the same name spools to a new temp file
Store overwrites the first mapping; first file is orphaned
Close removes only values still in the map

finding.guards_checked: Declared-size limits apply to each entry but not to the cumulative count of temp files. Low severity: disk leak per opened file, bounded by the declared-size limit.
